response.rationale: A and B describe the same capability: domain error types that signal when a business rule is broken. Both point to the same domain error classes by the same node ids: ValidationError (a1528852461831a2), ForbiddenError (eda714dca104af35), NotFoundError (1d689d7aed6f811c) and ConflictError (97d78fc7fa6c1e13), each written as an empty Error subclass, e.g. 'export class ValidationError extends Error {}'. A's scope is slightly wider. It adds the presentation-layer UnauthorizedError and puts 'access' in its name. That access part is already covered by ForbiddenError, which B also includes. Their community and component groupings differ, but the error classes at the core of each are the same.
